## College career
Towns shooting a free throw against the Florida Gators in 2015
In his freshman year, Kentucky used a unique "platoon system" that limited the minutes of each player, and he subsequently averaged 10.3 points and 6.7 rebounds in 21.1 minutes per game.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-17) He studied kinesiology in his one year at Kentucky, and hopes to become a doctor after his basketball career.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-18) Though he left Kentucky for the NBA, Towns enrolled in online courses, and hopes to earn his degree.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-schonbrun-19) He was named a second-team All-American by the Associated Press and NABC, and a third-team All-American by _The Sporting News_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-22) Throughout the 2014–15 season, Towns was often ranked behind [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball "Duke Blue Devils men's basketball") center Jahlil Okafor as a draft prospect. However, due to strong play in the NCAA Tournament, and a growing consensus that Towns was a better defensive player and had an opportunity to become a better offensive player as well, Towns overtook Okafor in most draft rankings.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-23)
On April 9, 2015, Towns and fellow Kentucky teammates Andrew Harrison, Aaron Harrison, Dakari Johnson, Devin Booker, Trey Lyles and Willie Cauley-Stein, all declared for the 2015 NBA draft.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-24)

## Professional career
### Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2024)
#### Rookie of the Year (2015–2016)
On June 25, 2015, Towns was selected by the Minnesota Timberwolves with the first overall pick in the 2015 NBA draft.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-25) He signed his rookie scale contract with the Timberwolves on July 7,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-26) and made his NBA debut in the Timberwolves' season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers on October 28, recording 14 points and 12 rebounds as a starter in a 112–111 win.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-27) In the following game on October 30 against the Denver Nuggets, his 28 points and 14 rebounds propelled the Timberwolves to their first 2–0 start with two wins on the road in team history.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-28) Over his first 13 games of the season, Towns averaged 16.0 points and 10.4 rebounds per game. Those numbers dropped, however, to 8.4 points and 6.0 rebounds over the next five games.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-29) Despite this, on December 3, he was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for November, becoming just the seventh Timberwolves player to win NBA Rookie of the Month honors.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-30)

## Professional career
### Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2024)
#### Rookie of the Year (2015–2016)
On January 20, 2016, Towns had a season-best game with 27 points and career highs of 17 rebounds and six blocks in a 106–94 loss to the Dallas Mavericks.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-31) On January 29, he recorded 32 points and 12 rebounds in a loss to the Utah Jazz, becoming the youngest player to have 30 points and 10 rebounds in a game since Kevin Durant did so in 2008.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-32) On February 2, he was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for January—his third consecutive rookie of the month honor.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-33) On February 10, he scored a then career-high 35 points in a 117–112 win over the Toronto Raptors.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-35) Three days later, he won the 2016 NBA All-Star Weekend Skills Challenge over point guard Isaiah Thomas, becoming the tallest, heaviest, and youngest winner of the event.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-36) On March 3, named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for February, joining teammate Andrew Wiggins (November, December 2014, January, February 2015) as the second player in Wolves history to earn NBA Rookie of the Month honors in four consecutive months.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-37)

## Professional career
### Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2024)
#### Rookie of the Year (2015–2016)
On March 25, Towns grabbed 10 rebounds against the Washington Wizards, setting a Minnesota rookie rebounding record, pushing his season total to 741 and passing Kevin Love's record of 734.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-38) On April 7, he recorded his 50th double-double of the season with 17 points and 10 rebounds in a 105–97 win over the Sacramento Kings.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-39) Four days later, in a loss to the Houston Rockets, Towns passed Christian Laettner for the franchise's rookie scoring record with 1,475 points.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-40) Earlier that day, he was named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, April 4 through Sunday, April 10.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-41) Towns played and started in all 82 games for the Timberwolves in 2015–16, averaging 18.3 points and 10.5 rebounds per game; he subsequently earned unanimous NBA Rookie of the Year honors.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-42) Towns earned Western Conference Rookie of the Month honors in each of the season's six months, becoming the first Timberwolves player to do so. In addition, he became just the fifth unanimous NBA Rookie of the Year, and with teammate Andrew Wiggins winning the award in 2014–15, Minnesota became the first team with back-to-back Rookie of the Year winners since the Buffalo Braves in 1972–73 (Bob McAdoo) and 1973–74 (Ernie DiGregorio), as well as the first team with back-to-back No.

## College career
Towns shooting a free throw against the Florida Gators in 2015
In his freshman year, Kentucky used a unique "platoon system" that limited the minutes of each player, and he subsequently averaged 10.3 points and 6.7 rebounds in 21.1 minutes per game.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-17) He studied kinesiology in his one year at Kentucky, and hopes to become a doctor after his basketball career.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-18) Though he left Kentucky for the NBA, Towns enrolled in online courses, and hopes to earn his degree.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-schonbrun-19) He was named a second-team All-American by the Associated Press and NABC, and a third-team All-American by _The Sporting News_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-22) Throughout the 2014–15 season, Towns was often ranked behind [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball "Duke Blue Devils men's basketball") center Jahlil Okafor as a draft prospect. However, due to strong play in the NCAA Tournament, and a growing consensus that Towns was a better defensive player and had an opportunity to become a better offensive player as well, Towns overtook Okafor in most draft rankings.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-23)
On April 9, 2015, Towns and fellow Kentucky teammates Andrew Harrison, Aaron Harrison, Dakari Johnson, Devin Booker, Trey Lyles and Willie Cauley-Stein, all declared for the 2015 NBA draft.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-24)
texts.8:
## Professional career
### Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2024)
#### Rookie of the Year (2015–2016)
On June 25, 2015, Towns was selected by the Minnesota Timberwolves with the first overall pick in the 2015 NBA draft.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-25) He signed his rookie scale contract with the Timberwolves on July 7,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-26) and made his NBA debut in the Timberwolves' season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers on October 28, recording 14 points and 12 rebounds as a starter in a 112–111 win.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-27) In the following game on October 30 against the Denver Nuggets, his 28 points and 14 rebounds propelled the Timberwolves to their first 2–0 start with two wins on the road in team history.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-28) Over his first 13 games of the season, Towns averaged 16.0 points and 10.4 rebounds per game. Those numbers dropped, however, to 8.4 points and 6.0 rebounds over the next five games.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-29) Despite this, on December 3, he was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for November, becoming just the seventh Timberwolves player to win NBA Rookie of the Month honors.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-30)
texts.9:
## Professional career
### Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2024)
#### Rookie of the Year (2015–2016)
On January 20, 2016, Towns had a season-best game with 27 points and career highs of 17 rebounds and six blocks in a 106–94 loss to the Dallas Mavericks.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-31) On January 29, he recorded 32 points and 12 rebounds in a loss to the Utah Jazz, becoming the youngest player to have 30 points and 10 rebounds in a game since Kevin Durant did so in 2008.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-32) On February 2, he was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for January—his third consecutive rookie of the month honor.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-33) On February 10, he scored a then career-high 35 points in a 117–112 win over the Toronto Raptors.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-35) Three days later, he won the 2016 NBA All-Star Weekend Skills Challenge over point guard Isaiah Thomas, becoming the tallest, heaviest, and youngest winner of the event.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-36) On March 3, named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for February, joining teammate Andrew Wiggins (November, December 2014, January, February 2015) as the second player in Wolves history to earn NBA Rookie of the Month honors in four consecutive months.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-37)
texts.10:
## Professional career
### Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2024)
#### Rookie of the Year (2015–2016)
On March 25, Towns grabbed 10 rebounds against the Washington Wizards, setting a Minnesota rookie rebounding record, pushing his season total to 741 and passing Kevin Love's record of 734.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-38) On April 7, he recorded his 50th double-double of the season with 17 points and 10 rebounds in a 105–97 win over the Sacramento Kings.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-39) Four days later, in a loss to the Houston Rockets, Towns passed Christian Laettner for the franchise's rookie scoring record with 1,475 points.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-40) Earlier that day, he was named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, April 4 through Sunday, April 10.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-41) Towns played and started in all 82 games for the Timberwolves in 2015–16, averaging 18.3 points and 10.5 rebounds per game; he subsequently earned unanimous NBA Rookie of the Year honors.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-42) Towns earned Western Conference Rookie of the Month honors in each of the season's six months, becoming the first Timberwolves player to do so. In addition, he became just the fifth unanimous NBA Rookie of the Year, and with teammate Andrew Wiggins winning the award in 2014–15, Minnesota became the first team with back-to-back Rookie of the Year winners since the Buffalo Braves in 1972–73 (Bob McAdoo) and 1973–74 (Ernie DiGregorio), as well as the first team with back-to-back No.

## College career
Towns shooting a free throw against the Florida Gators in 2015
In his freshman year, Kentucky used a unique "platoon system" that limited the minutes of each player, and he subsequently averaged 10.3 points and 6.7 rebounds in 21.1 minutes per game.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-17) He studied kinesiology in his one year at Kentucky, and hopes to become a doctor after his basketball career.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-18) Though he left Kentucky for the NBA, Towns enrolled in online courses, and hopes to earn his degree.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-schonbrun-19) He was named a second-team All-American by the Associated Press and NABC, and a third-team All-American by _The Sporting News_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-22) Throughout the 2014–15 season, Towns was often ranked behind [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball "Duke Blue Devils men's basketball") center Jahlil Okafor as a draft prospect. However, due to strong play in the NCAA Tournament, and a growing consensus that Towns was a better defensive player and had an opportunity to become a better offensive player as well, Towns overtook Okafor in most draft rankings.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-23)
On April 9, 2015, Towns and fellow Kentucky teammates Andrew Harrison, Aaron Harrison, Dakari Johnson, Devin Booker, Trey Lyles and Willie Cauley-Stein, all declared for the 2015 NBA draft.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-24)

## Professional career
### Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2024)
#### Rookie of the Year (2015–2016)
On June 25, 2015, Towns was selected by the Minnesota Timberwolves with the first overall pick in the 2015 NBA draft.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-25) He signed his rookie scale contract with the Timberwolves on July 7,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-26) and made his NBA debut in the Timberwolves' season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers on October 28, recording 14 points and 12 rebounds as a starter in a 112–111 win.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-27) In the following game on October 30 against the Denver Nuggets, his 28 points and 14 rebounds propelled the Timberwolves to their first 2–0 start with two wins on the road in team history.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-28) Over his first 13 games of the season, Towns averaged 16.0 points and 10.4 rebounds per game. Those numbers dropped, however, to 8.4 points and 6.0 rebounds over the next five games.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-29) Despite this, on December 3, he was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for November, becoming just the seventh Timberwolves player to win NBA Rookie of the Month honors.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-30)

## Professional career
### Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2024)
#### Rookie of the Year (2015–2016)
On January 20, 2016, Towns had a season-best game with 27 points and career highs of 17 rebounds and six blocks in a 106–94 loss to the Dallas Mavericks.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-31) On January 29, he recorded 32 points and 12 rebounds in a loss to the Utah Jazz, becoming the youngest player to have 30 points and 10 rebounds in a game since Kevin Durant did so in 2008.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-32) On February 2, he was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for January—his third consecutive rookie of the month honor.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-33) On February 10, he scored a then career-high 35 points in a 117–112 win over the Toronto Raptors.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-35) Three days later, he won the 2016 NBA All-Star Weekend Skills Challenge over point guard Isaiah Thomas, becoming the tallest, heaviest, and youngest winner of the event.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-36) On March 3, named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for February, joining teammate Andrew Wiggins (November, December 2014, January, February 2015) as the second player in Wolves history to earn NBA Rookie of the Month honors in four consecutive months.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-37)

## Professional career
### Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2024)
#### Rookie of the Year (2015–2016)
On March 25, Towns grabbed 10 rebounds against the Washington Wizards, setting a Minnesota rookie rebounding record, pushing his season total to 741 and passing Kevin Love's record of 734.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-38) On April 7, he recorded his 50th double-double of the season with 17 points and 10 rebounds in a 105–97 win over the Sacramento Kings.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-39) Four days later, in a loss to the Houston Rockets, Towns passed Christian Laettner for the franchise's rookie scoring record with 1,475 points.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-40) Earlier that day, he was named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, April 4 through Sunday, April 10.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-41) Towns played and started in all 82 games for the Timberwolves in 2015–16, averaging 18.3 points and 10.5 rebounds per game; he subsequently earned unanimous NBA Rookie of the Year honors.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns#cite_note-42) Towns earned Western Conference Rookie of the Month honors in each of the season's six months, becoming the first Timberwolves player to do so. # NBA birthdays: Players born on August 1
With a player born on each day, our birthday series continues with the NBA players born on August 1.
Joel Bartilotta, Rotowire.com
September 24, 2025 3:17 PM
Scottie Barnes is among the players born on August 1.
With over 5,000 players in NBA history, at least one player was born on every day of the calendar year – including four leap day ballers. Our day-by-day breakdown of the players born on each day of the year continues.
Below are the most notable NBA players born on August 1.
* * *

# NBA birthdays: Players born on August 1
### **Scottie Barnes (2001)**
Barnes rose up draft boards to become the fourth overall pick in the 2021 NBA Draft and has made the Raptors look smart for making that selection. A defensive standout, Barnes won Rookie of the Year in his debut season, averaging 15.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.7 blocks per game.
He posted similar averages in his second season but made a significant jump in the 2023-24 season. That was Barnes’ first All-Star appearance as he posted a career-high 19.9 points per game to go with 8.2 rebounds, 6.1 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.5 blocks. Barnes is becoming one of the best all-around contributors already as he enters his age-24 season in 2025.

# NBA birthdays: Players born on August 1
### **Kiki Vandeweghe (1958)**
Vandeweghe was one of the best forwards in the NBA during the 1980s. Selected 11th overall in the 1980 NBA Draft by the Dallas Mavericks, a trade sent him to the Denver Nuggets, where he would develop into one of their best players. Kiki averaged at least 20 points per game for seven seasons. His stint in Denver was highlighted by a pair of All-Star nods in 1983 and 1984.
Vandeweghe then had a five-year stint with the Trail Blazers following his departure from the Nuggets and had several more standout seasons. A four-year run with the Knicks followed by a one-year stop with the Clippers rounded out Vandeweghe’s strong 13-year career.

texts.4:
# NBA birthdays: Players born on August 1
### **Scottie Barnes (2001)**
Barnes rose up draft boards to become the fourth overall pick in the 2021 NBA Draft and has made the Raptors look smart for making that selection. A defensive standout, Barnes won Rookie of the Year in his debut season, averaging 15.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.7 blocks per game.
He posted similar averages in his second season but made a significant jump in the 2023-24 season. That was Barnes’ first All-Star appearance as he posted a career-high 19.9 points per game to go with 8.2 rebounds, 6.1 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.5 blocks. Barnes is becoming one of the best all-around contributors already as he enters his age-24 season in 2025.
texts.5:
# NBA birthdays: Players born on August 1
### **Kiki Vandeweghe (1958)**
Vandeweghe was one of the best forwards in the NBA during the 1980s. Selected 11th overall in the 1980 NBA Draft by the Dallas Mavericks, a trade sent him to the Denver Nuggets, where he would develop into one of their best players. Kiki averaged at least 20 points per game for seven seasons. His stint in Denver was highlighted by a pair of All-Star nods in 1983 and 1984.
Vandeweghe then had a five-year stint with the Trail Blazers following his departure from the Nuggets and had several more standout seasons. A four-year run with the Knicks followed by a one-year stop with the Clippers rounded out Vandeweghe’s strong 13-year career.

# NBA birthdays: Players born on August 1
### **Scottie Barnes (2001)**
Barnes rose up draft boards to become the fourth overall pick in the 2021 NBA Draft and has made the Raptors look smart for making that selection. A defensive standout, Barnes won Rookie of the Year in his debut season, averaging 15.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.7 blocks per game.
He posted similar averages in his second season but made a significant jump in the 2023-24 season. That was Barnes’ first All-Star appearance as he posted a career-high 19.9 points per game to go with 8.2 rebounds, 6.1 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.5 blocks. Barnes is becoming one of the best all-around contributors already as he enters his age-24 season in 2025.

# NBA birthdays: Players born on August 1
### **Kiki Vandeweghe (1958)**
Vandeweghe was one of the best forwards in the NBA during the 1980s. Selected 11th overall in the 1980 NBA Draft by the Dallas Mavericks, a trade sent him to the Denver Nuggets, where he would develop into one of their best players. Kiki averaged at least 20 points per game for seven seasons. His stint in Denver was highlighted by a pair of All-Star nods in 1983 and 1984.
Vandeweghe then had a five-year stint with the Trail Blazers following his departure from the Nuggets and had several more standout seasons. A four-year run with the Knicks followed by a one-year stop with the Clippers rounded out Vandeweghe’s strong 13-year career.

The **2024 NBA draft** was the 78th edition of the National Basketball Association's annual draft. Unlike recent years, the 2024 draft took place over two nights. This was the first NBA draft held over multiple nights since the current two-round format debuted in 1989.
The first round of the draft took place on June 26, 2024, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York, while the second round took place on June 27 at ESPN's Seaport District Studios in Manhattan. The time between second-round picks expanded from two minutes to four.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-2) For the third year in a row, the draft had 58 picks instead of the typical 60: both the Philadelphia 76ers and the Phoenix Suns lost second-round picks for violations of the NBA's tampering rules during free agency.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-76ersTamper-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-SunsTamper-4)

The first overall selection was owned by the Atlanta Hawks, which they used to select French forward Zaccharie Risacher, making him the second consecutive French player to be drafted with the number one pick, after the San Antonio Spurs had picked Victor Wembanyama in the previous year's edition.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:0-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) France became the second nation (after the U.S.) to have at least three native players picked in the top 10 spots of any NBA draft following the selections of Risacher, Alex Sarr, and Tidjane Salaün,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:0-5)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) as well as the second nation (after the U.S.) to have two native players get selected with the first and second overall picks.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) The eventual Rookie of the Year would be fourth pick Stephon Castle for the Spurs.
Bronny James, the son of LeBron James, was selected 55th overall in the second round and would become the first player in NBA history to play alongside his father.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-8)

The **2024 NBA draft** was the 78th edition of the National Basketball Association's annual draft. Unlike recent years, the 2024 draft took place over two nights. This was the first NBA draft held over multiple nights since the current two-round format debuted in 1989.
The first round of the draft took place on June 26, 2024, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York, while the second round took place on June 27 at ESPN's Seaport District Studios in Manhattan. The time between second-round picks expanded from two minutes to four.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-2) For the third year in a row, the draft had 58 picks instead of the typical 60: both the Philadelphia 76ers and the Phoenix Suns lost second-round picks for violations of the NBA's tampering rules during free agency.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-76ersTamper-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-SunsTamper-4)
texts.1:
The first overall selection was owned by the Atlanta Hawks, which they used to select French forward Zaccharie Risacher, making him the second consecutive French player to be drafted with the number one pick, after the San Antonio Spurs had picked Victor Wembanyama in the previous year's edition.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:0-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) France became the second nation (after the U.S.) to have at least three native players picked in the top 10 spots of any NBA draft following the selections of Risacher, Alex Sarr, and Tidjane Salaün,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:0-5)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) as well as the second nation (after the U.S.) to have two native players get selected with the first and second overall picks.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) The eventual Rookie of the Year would be fourth pick Stephon Castle for the Spurs.
Bronny James, the son of LeBron James, was selected 55th overall in the second round and would become the first player in NBA history to play alongside his father.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-8)

The **2024 NBA draft** was the 78th edition of the National Basketball Association's annual draft. Unlike recent years, the 2024 draft took place over two nights. This was the first NBA draft held over multiple nights since the current two-round format debuted in 1989.
The first round of the draft took place on June 26, 2024, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York, while the second round took place on June 27 at ESPN's Seaport District Studios in Manhattan. The time between second-round picks expanded from two minutes to four.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-2) For the third year in a row, the draft had 58 picks instead of the typical 60: both the Philadelphia 76ers and the Phoenix Suns lost second-round picks for violations of the NBA's tampering rules during free agency.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-76ersTamper-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-SunsTamper-4)

The first overall selection was owned by the Atlanta Hawks, which they used to select French forward Zaccharie Risacher, making him the second consecutive French player to be drafted with the number one pick, after the San Antonio Spurs had picked Victor Wembanyama in the previous year's edition.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:0-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) France became the second nation (after the U.S.) to have at least three native players picked in the top 10 spots of any NBA draft following the selections of Risacher, Alex Sarr, and Tidjane Salaün,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:0-5)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) as well as the second nation (after the U.S.) to have two native players get selected with the first and second overall picks.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) The eventual Rookie of the Year would be fourth pick Stephon Castle for the Spurs.
Bronny James, the son of LeBron James, was selected 55th overall in the second round and would become the first player in NBA history to play alongside his father.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-8)

**Scott Wayne Barnes Jr.** (born August 1, 2001) is an American professional basketball player for the Toronto Raptors of the National Basketball Association (NBA). Widely regarded as one of the best defenders in the league, he is known for his versatility, shot-blocking, and playmaking.
Barnes attended Cardinal Newman High School in his hometown of West Palm Beach, Florida, before transferring to NSU University School. He later attended Montverde Academy, where he was rated a consensus five-star recruit and among the top players in the 2020 class by major recruiting services in his senior year. He played college basketball for the [Florida State Seminoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Seminoles_men's_basketball "Florida State Seminoles men's basketball") and was named the [conference rookie of the year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Rookie_of_the_Year "Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year") in 2021.
Selected with the fourth overall pick by the Raptors in the 2021 NBA draft, Barnes was named the NBA Rookie of the Year in 2022. After a relatively disappointing second season, he had a breakout year in 2024, when he received his first All-Star selection and the Raptors pivoted to him as their franchise player. As the Raptors became competitive again after a rebuild, Barnes received his second All-Star selection and his first on an All-Defensive Team in 2026. He is regarded as a versatile player, capable of playmaking, ball-handling, and many defensive functions, although his jump shot has been an area of criticism.

## Early life
Barnes was born on August 1, 2001,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:50-1) in West Palm Beach, Florida, and was raised alongside three siblings by their mother Kathalyn Wilkins.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:13-2) Barnes described his upbringing as "pretty hard" as his family did not have stable housing and lived in troublesome neighborhoods.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3) He began playing organized basketball in the third grade in a Salvation Army league, with a team composed mostly of fourth-graders.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:47-4) He also played pick-up at local gyms against opponents much older than him, who he credited for improving his perception and knowledge of the game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:39-5)

## Early life
As a fifth-grader Barnes caught the attention of Amateur Athletic Union (AAU) youth basketball coach John Simpson, who was invited to join his team, the Wellington Wolves.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:13-2) Simpson and his son Jason developed a close relationship with Barnes, who soon moved in with them in the affluent village of Wellington so he could reduce the burden on his mother.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:14-6)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3) With Barnes, the Wolves went from what Simpson described as a purely casual team to participating in national tournaments.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:39-5) Already gifted in height, Barnes refined his athleticism and overall game with the Wolves, and by the end of seventh grade he was dominating his opponents.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:14-6)

## High school career
Barnes at the Nike EYBL in 2019
As a freshman in 2016, Barnes played basketball for Cardinal Newman High School in West Palm Beach.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3) He earned All-Area second team and MaxPreps Freshman All-American honors after leading Newman to a 19–8 record and the 5A regional semifinals.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-wagner-7)

**Scott Wayne Barnes Jr.** (born August 1, 2001) is an American professional basketball player for the Toronto Raptors of the National Basketball Association (NBA). Widely regarded as one of the best defenders in the league, he is known for his versatility, shot-blocking, and playmaking.
Barnes attended Cardinal Newman High School in his hometown of West Palm Beach, Florida, before transferring to NSU University School. He later attended Montverde Academy, where he was rated a consensus five-star recruit and among the top players in the 2020 class by major recruiting services in his senior year. He played college basketball for the [Florida State Seminoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Seminoles_men's_basketball "Florida State Seminoles men's basketball") and was named the [conference rookie of the year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Rookie_of_the_Year "Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year") in 2021.
Selected with the fourth overall pick by the Raptors in the 2021 NBA draft, Barnes was named the NBA Rookie of the Year in 2022. After a relatively disappointing second season, he had a breakout year in 2024, when he received his first All-Star selection and the Raptors pivoted to him as their franchise player. As the Raptors became competitive again after a rebuild, Barnes received his second All-Star selection and his first on an All-Defensive Team in 2026. He is regarded as a versatile player, capable of playmaking, ball-handling, and many defensive functions, although his jump shot has been an area of criticism.
texts.3:
## Early life
Barnes was born on August 1, 2001,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:50-1) in West Palm Beach, Florida, and was raised alongside three siblings by their mother Kathalyn Wilkins.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:13-2) Barnes described his upbringing as "pretty hard" as his family did not have stable housing and lived in troublesome neighborhoods.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3) He began playing organized basketball in the third grade in a Salvation Army league, with a team composed mostly of fourth-graders.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:47-4) He also played pick-up at local gyms against opponents much older than him, who he credited for improving his perception and knowledge of the game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:39-5)
texts.4:
## Early life
As a fifth-grader Barnes caught the attention of Amateur Athletic Union (AAU) youth basketball coach John Simpson, who was invited to join his team, the Wellington Wolves.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:13-2) Simpson and his son Jason developed a close relationship with Barnes, who soon moved in with them in the affluent village of Wellington so he could reduce the burden on his mother.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:14-6)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3) With Barnes, the Wolves went from what Simpson described as a purely casual team to participating in national tournaments.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:39-5) Already gifted in height, Barnes refined his athleticism and overall game with the Wolves, and by the end of seventh grade he was dominating his opponents.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:14-6)
texts.5:
## High school career
Barnes at the Nike EYBL in 2019
As a freshman in 2016, Barnes played basketball for Cardinal Newman High School in West Palm Beach.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3) He earned All-Area second team and MaxPreps Freshman All-American honors after leading Newman to a 19–8 record and the 5A regional semifinals.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-wagner-7)

**Scott Wayne Barnes Jr.** (born August 1, 2001) is an American professional basketball player for the Toronto Raptors of the National Basketball Association (NBA). Widely regarded as one of the best defenders in the league, he is known for his versatility, shot-blocking, and playmaking.
Barnes attended Cardinal Newman High School in his hometown of West Palm Beach, Florida, before transferring to NSU University School. He later attended Montverde Academy, where he was rated a consensus five-star recruit and among the top players in the 2020 class by major recruiting services in his senior year. He played college basketball for the [Florida State Seminoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Seminoles_men's_basketball "Florida State Seminoles men's basketball") and was named the [conference rookie of the year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Rookie_of_the_Year "Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year") in 2021.
Selected with the fourth overall pick by the Raptors in the 2021 NBA draft, Barnes was named the NBA Rookie of the Year in 2022. After a relatively disappointing second season, he had a breakout year in 2024, when he received his first All-Star selection and the Raptors pivoted to him as their franchise player. As the Raptors became competitive again after a rebuild, Barnes received his second All-Star selection and his first on an All-Defensive Team in 2026. He is regarded as a versatile player, capable of playmaking, ball-handling, and many defensive functions, although his jump shot has been an area of criticism.

## Early life
Barnes was born on August 1, 2001,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:50-1) in West Palm Beach, Florida, and was raised alongside three siblings by their mother Kathalyn Wilkins.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:13-2) Barnes described his upbringing as "pretty hard" as his family did not have stable housing and lived in troublesome neighborhoods.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3) He began playing organized basketball in the third grade in a Salvation Army league, with a team composed mostly of fourth-graders.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:47-4) He also played pick-up at local gyms against opponents much older than him, who he credited for improving his perception and knowledge of the game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:39-5)

## Early life
As a fifth-grader Barnes caught the attention of Amateur Athletic Union (AAU) youth basketball coach John Simpson, who was invited to join his team, the Wellington Wolves.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:13-2) Simpson and his son Jason developed a close relationship with Barnes, who soon moved in with them in the affluent village of Wellington so he could reduce the burden on his mother.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:14-6)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3) With Barnes, the Wolves went from what Simpson described as a purely casual team to participating in national tournaments.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:39-5) Already gifted in height, Barnes refined his athleticism and overall game with the Wolves, and by the end of seventh grade he was dominating his opponents.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:14-6)

## High school career
Barnes at the Nike EYBL in 2019
As a freshman in 2016, Barnes played basketball for Cardinal Newman High School in West Palm Beach.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-:15-3) He earned All-Area second team and MaxPreps Freshman All-American honors after leading Newman to a 19–8 record and the 5A regional semifinals.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Barnes#cite_note-wagner-7)

While playing for the [Golden Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Golden_Bears_men's_basketball "California Golden Bears men's basketball") in [2015–16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_California_Golden_Bears_men's_basketball_team "2015–16 California Golden Bears men's basketball team"), Brown averaged 14.6 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 2.0 assists in 27.6 minutes per game over 34 games.

## College career
He had his best scoring games on November 27, 2015, against [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond_Spiders_men's_basketball "Richmond Spiders men's basketball") and January 27, 2016, against [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Utes_men's_basketball "Utah Utes men's basketball"), recording 27 points in each game.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-18) Brown had a season-high 11 rebounds twice during victories on November 23, 2015, against [Sam Houston State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Houston_State_Bearkats_men's_basketball "Sam Houston State Bearkats men's basketball") and on January 1, 2016, against [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Buffaloes_men's_basketball "Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-20) On January 23, 2016,

## College career
he recorded a season-high seven assists to go along with 15 points in a narrow 74–73 victory over [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Arizona Wildcats men's basketball").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-21) Brown earned first-team [All-Pac-12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_All-Pac-12_Conference_men's_basketball_teams "List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams") honors and was named the [Pac-12 Freshman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pac-12_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Freshman_of_the_Year "Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-23)

## Professional career
### Boston Celtics (2016–2026)
#### 2016–17 season: Rookie season
Brown in 2017
On June 23, 2016, Brown was selected by the Boston Celtics with the third overall pick in the 2016 NBA draft.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-Washburn-24) On July 27, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Celtics after averaging 16.0 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.3 steals in six Summer League games.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-25)
Brown made his debut for the Celtics on October 26, 2016, in the season-opening 122–117 victory over the Brooklyn Nets, scoring nine points on 3-for-4 shooting while also adding two blocks in 19-plus minutes.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-26) In his first career start on November 3, Brown scored 19 points in a 128–122 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-27) On January 27, 2017, he scored a then career-high 20 points in a 128–98 victory over the Orlando Magic.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-28)

## Professional career
### Boston Celtics (2016–2026)
#### 2016–17 season: Rookie season
Brown helped the Celtics claim the top seed in the Eastern Conference before helping them advance to the Eastern Conference Finals, where the Celtics lost to the Cavaliers in five games.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-29) Brown had a productive rookie season, with his role off the bench continuing to develop as the year went on. Brown averaged 17.2 minutes on the floor, 6.6 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 0.8 assists in 78 games and 20 starts.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-30) He was named to the NBA All-Rookie Second Team at the end of the season.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown#cite_note-31)

**Anthony Jermal Edwards** (born August 5, 2001), nicknamed "**Ant-Man**" or simply "**Ant**",[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Basketball-Reference.com-1) is an American professional basketball player for the Minnesota Timberwolves of the National Basketball Association (NBA). A shooting guard, Edwards played college basketball for the Georgia Bulldogs and was selected with the first overall pick by the Timberwolves in the 2020 NBA draft. He is a four-time NBA All-Star, a two-time All-NBA Second Team selection, and won a gold medal on the [2024 U.S. Olympic team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_men's_Olympic_basketball_team "2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-2)
Edwards finished his high school career at Holy Spirit Preparatory School in his hometown of Atlanta, Georgia, where he was rated a consensus five-star recruit and one of the best players in the 2019 class by major recruiting services. As a senior, he earned [McDonald's All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald's_All-American_Game "McDonald's All-American Game") and _USA Today_ All-USA first team honors. He committed to play college basketball for Georgia, becoming the highest-rated recruit to do so, and was named [SEC Freshman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Rookie_of_the_Year "Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year") after his freshman season with the team.

## Early life
Edwards spent his early life in Oakland City, Atlanta, Georgia.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-3) When he was three years old, he was given the nickname "Ant-Man" by his father. For much of his childhood, Edwards played football in the running back, quarterback, and cornerback positions.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4) He played youth football for the Atlanta Vikings and became one of the best Pop Warner running backs in the country by age 10.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Jones-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Westerholm-6) Edwards switched his focus to basketball because he "thought it looked more fun" after watching his brothers play the sport. He often played basketball with his brothers at their grandmother's house. Entering ninth grade, he began training with Justin Holland, a former college basketball player for Liberty and an Atlanta-based basketball trainer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4)

## Early life
Edwards's mother, Yvette, and grandmother, Shirley, both died of cancer during an eight-month span in 2015, when he was in eighth grade. He has worn the No. 5 basketball jersey since high school to honor them, as they both died on the fifth day of the month.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-selfmade-7) After their deaths, Edwards was raised by his sister, Antoinette, and brother, Antoine, who shared legal custody of him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Towers-8) In high school, Edwards frequently worked as an instructor at youth camps.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Pourtout-9) He intended to major in marketing while attending the University of Georgia.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-bio-10)
During his childhood, Edwards also starred in baseball, often acting as his team's fourth or fifth hitter in the batting order. He has jokingly said he was very skilled at a variety of sports when he was younger. He owns two dogs and has also expressed his affinity for lions, although he does not believe he has the requisite space to care for one.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-11)

## High school
Due to his success with the Atlanta Xpress 15-under Amateur Athletic Union team, Edwards was considered a four-star recruit by Rivals in 2016.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-McDonald-12) He began playing high school basketball for Therrell High School in Atlanta as a member of the 2019 class.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Krohn-13) In early January 2017, Edwards transferred to Holy Spirit Preparatory School in Atlanta and reclassified to the 2020 class. He made the move in an effort to improve his academic performance, since Holy Spirit Preparatory had "small class sizes and support to help that."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Neysmith-14)

**Anthony Jermal Edwards** (born August 5, 2001), nicknamed "**Ant-Man**" or simply "**Ant**",[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Basketball-Reference.com-1) is an American professional basketball player for the Minnesota Timberwolves of the National Basketball Association (NBA). A shooting guard, Edwards played college basketball for the Georgia Bulldogs and was selected with the first overall pick by the Timberwolves in the 2020 NBA draft. He is a four-time NBA All-Star, a two-time All-NBA Second Team selection, and won a gold medal on the [2024 U.S. Olympic team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_men's_Olympic_basketball_team "2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-2)
Edwards finished his high school career at Holy Spirit Preparatory School in his hometown of Atlanta, Georgia, where he was rated a consensus five-star recruit and one of the best players in the 2019 class by major recruiting services. As a senior, he earned [McDonald's All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald's_All-American_Game "McDonald's All-American Game") and _USA Today_ All-USA first team honors. He committed to play college basketball for Georgia, becoming the highest-rated recruit to do so, and was named [SEC Freshman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Rookie_of_the_Year "Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year") after his freshman season with the team.

## Early life
Edwards spent his early life in Oakland City, Atlanta, Georgia.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-3) When he was three years old, he was given the nickname "Ant-Man" by his father. For much of his childhood, Edwards played football in the running back, quarterback, and cornerback positions.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4) He played youth football for the Atlanta Vikings and became one of the best Pop Warner running backs in the country by age 10.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Jones-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Westerholm-6) Edwards switched his focus to basketball because he "thought it looked more fun" after watching his brothers play the sport. He often played basketball with his brothers at their grandmother's house. Entering ninth grade, he began training with Justin Holland, a former college basketball player for Liberty and an Atlanta-based basketball trainer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4)
texts.4:
## Early life
Edwards's mother, Yvette, and grandmother, Shirley, both died of cancer during an eight-month span in 2015, when he was in eighth grade. He has worn the No. 5 basketball jersey since high school to honor them, as they both died on the fifth day of the month.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-selfmade-7) After their deaths, Edwards was raised by his sister, Antoinette, and brother, Antoine, who shared legal custody of him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Towers-8) In high school, Edwards frequently worked as an instructor at youth camps.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Pourtout-9) He intended to major in marketing while attending the University of Georgia.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-bio-10)
During his childhood, Edwards also starred in baseball, often acting as his team's fourth or fifth hitter in the batting order. He has jokingly said he was very skilled at a variety of sports when he was younger. He owns two dogs and has also expressed his affinity for lions, although he does not believe he has the requisite space to care for one.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-11)
texts.5:
## High school
Due to his success with the Atlanta Xpress 15-under Amateur Athletic Union team, Edwards was considered a four-star recruit by Rivals in 2016.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-McDonald-12) He began playing high school basketball for Therrell High School in Atlanta as a member of the 2019 class.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Krohn-13) In early January 2017, Edwards transferred to Holy Spirit Preparatory School in Atlanta and reclassified to the 2020 class. He made the move in an effort to improve his academic performance, since Holy Spirit Preparatory had "small class sizes and support to help that."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Neysmith-14)

**Anthony Jermal Edwards** (born August 5, 2001), nicknamed "**Ant-Man**" or simply "**Ant**",[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Basketball-Reference.com-1) is an American professional basketball player for the Minnesota Timberwolves of the National Basketball Association (NBA). A shooting guard, Edwards played college basketball for the Georgia Bulldogs and was selected with the first overall pick by the Timberwolves in the 2020 NBA draft. He is a four-time NBA All-Star, a two-time All-NBA Second Team selection, and won a gold medal on the [2024 U.S. Olympic team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_men's_Olympic_basketball_team "2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-2)
Edwards finished his high school career at Holy Spirit Preparatory School in his hometown of Atlanta, Georgia, where he was rated a consensus five-star recruit and one of the best players in the 2019 class by major recruiting services. As a senior, he earned [McDonald's All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald's_All-American_Game "McDonald's All-American Game") and _USA Today_ All-USA first team honors. He committed to play college basketball for Georgia, becoming the highest-rated recruit to do so, and was named [SEC Freshman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Rookie_of_the_Year "Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year") after his freshman season with the team.

## Early life
Edwards spent his early life in Oakland City, Atlanta, Georgia.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-3) When he was three years old, he was given the nickname "Ant-Man" by his father. For much of his childhood, Edwards played football in the running back, quarterback, and cornerback positions.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4) He played youth football for the Atlanta Vikings and became one of the best Pop Warner running backs in the country by age 10.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Jones-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Westerholm-6) Edwards switched his focus to basketball because he "thought it looked more fun" after watching his brothers play the sport. He often played basketball with his brothers at their grandmother's house. Entering ninth grade, he began training with Justin Holland, a former college basketball player for Liberty and an Atlanta-based basketball trainer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4)

## Early life
Edwards's mother, Yvette, and grandmother, Shirley, both died of cancer during an eight-month span in 2015, when he was in eighth grade. He has worn the No. 5 basketball jersey since high school to honor them, as they both died on the fifth day of the month.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-selfmade-7) After their deaths, Edwards was raised by his sister, Antoinette, and brother, Antoine, who shared legal custody of him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Towers-8) In high school, Edwards frequently worked as an instructor at youth camps.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Pourtout-9) He intended to major in marketing while attending the University of Georgia.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-bio-10)
During his childhood, Edwards also starred in baseball, often acting as his team's fourth or fifth hitter in the batting order. He has jokingly said he was very skilled at a variety of sports when he was younger. He owns two dogs and has also expressed his affinity for lions, although he does not believe he has the requisite space to care for one.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-11)

## High school
Due to his success with the Atlanta Xpress 15-under Amateur Athletic Union team, Edwards was considered a four-star recruit by Rivals in 2016.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-McDonald-12) He began playing high school basketball for Therrell High School in Atlanta as a member of the 2019 class.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Krohn-13) In early January 2017, Edwards transferred to Holy Spirit Preparatory School in Atlanta and reclassified to the 2020 class. He made the move in an effort to improve his academic performance, since Holy Spirit Preparatory had "small class sizes and support to help that."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Neysmith-14)

**Victor Nonga Wembanyama-de Fautereau-Vassel** ( _WEM-bən-YAH-mə_;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-1)French:[[viktɔʁ wɛmbanjama]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French"); born 4 January 2004), nicknamed "**Wemby**"[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-2) and "**the Alien**",[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-4) is a French professional basketball player for the San Antonio Spurs of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He was selected first overall by the Spurs in the 2023 NBA draft and is considered one of the best basketball prospects ever due to his rare combination of height, agility, and skills.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-5)
Wembanyama began his professional career at age 15 with Nanterre 92 of the LNB Pro A in 2019. Two years later, he moved to ASVEL and won the Pro A title in his only season with the team. In the 2022–23 season, Wembanyama signed with Metropolitans 92 and became the youngest player to win the Pro A MVP award, while earning Pro A Best Defender honours and leading the league in scoring, rebounds and blocks. He was unanimously named an LNB All-Star twice, winning the All-Star Game MVP once, and was a three-time Pro A Best Young Player from 2021 to 2023.

Following a historic rookie season in the NBA in which he led the league in blocks per game, Wembanyama was unanimously named the 2024NBA Rookie of the Year and became the first rookie and youngest player ever to be named to the All-Defensive First Team.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-espn_lopez-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-7) During the 2025–26 season, Wembanyama became the youngest and first unanimous winner of the Defensive Player of the Year award.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-9) That same year, he led the Spurs to the NBA Finals in his first postseason appearance.
Wembanyama also plays for the [French national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_men's_national_basketball_team "France men's national basketball team"), with whom he won a silver medal at the [2024 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament"). At the youth level, he led his team to two silver medals, including at the 2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup, where he set the FIBA record for blocks per game in a single tournament.

texts.2:
**Victor Nonga Wembanyama-de Fautereau-Vassel** ( _WEM-bən-YAH-mə_;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-1)French:[[viktɔʁ wɛmbanjama]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French"); born 4 January 2004), nicknamed "**Wemby**"[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-2) and "**the Alien**",[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-4) is a French professional basketball player for the San Antonio Spurs of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He was selected first overall by the Spurs in the 2023 NBA draft and is considered one of the best basketball prospects ever due to his rare combination of height, agility, and skills.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-5)
Wembanyama began his professional career at age 15 with Nanterre 92 of the LNB Pro A in 2019. Two years later, he moved to ASVEL and won the Pro A title in his only season with the team. In the 2022–23 season, Wembanyama signed with Metropolitans 92 and became the youngest player to win the Pro A MVP award, while earning Pro A Best Defender honours and leading the league in scoring, rebounds and blocks. He was unanimously named an LNB All-Star twice, winning the All-Star Game MVP once, and was a three-time Pro A Best Young Player from 2021 to 2023.
texts.3:
Following a historic rookie season in the NBA in which he led the league in blocks per game, Wembanyama was unanimously named the 2024NBA Rookie of the Year and became the first rookie and youngest player ever to be named to the All-Defensive First Team.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-espn_lopez-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-7) During the 2025–26 season, Wembanyama became the youngest and first unanimous winner of the Defensive Player of the Year award.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-9) That same year, he led the Spurs to the NBA Finals in his first postseason appearance.
Wembanyama also plays for the [French national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_men's_national_basketball_team "France men's national basketball team"), with whom he won a silver medal at the [2024 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament"). At the youth level, he led his team to two silver medals, including at the 2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup, where he set the FIBA record for blocks per game in a single tournament.

**Victor Nonga Wembanyama-de Fautereau-Vassel** ( _WEM-bən-YAH-mə_;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-1)French:[[viktɔʁ wɛmbanjama]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French"); born 4 January 2004), nicknamed "**Wemby**"[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-2) and "**the Alien**",[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-4) is a French professional basketball player for the San Antonio Spurs of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He was selected first overall by the Spurs in the 2023 NBA draft and is considered one of the best basketball prospects ever due to his rare combination of height, agility, and skills.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-5)
Wembanyama began his professional career at age 15 with Nanterre 92 of the LNB Pro A in 2019. Two years later, he moved to ASVEL and won the Pro A title in his only season with the team. In the 2022–23 season, Wembanyama signed with Metropolitans 92 and became the youngest player to win the Pro A MVP award, while earning Pro A Best Defender honours and leading the league in scoring, rebounds and blocks. He was unanimously named an LNB All-Star twice, winning the All-Star Game MVP once, and was a three-time Pro A Best Young Player from 2021 to 2023.

Following a historic rookie season in the NBA in which he led the league in blocks per game, Wembanyama was unanimously named the 2024NBA Rookie of the Year and became the first rookie and youngest player ever to be named to the All-Defensive First Team.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-espn_lopez-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-7) During the 2025–26 season, Wembanyama became the youngest and first unanimous winner of the Defensive Player of the Year award.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama#cite_note-9) That same year, he led the Spurs to the NBA Finals in his first postseason appearance.
Wembanyama also plays for the [French national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_men's_national_basketball_team "France men's national basketball team"), with whom he won a silver medal at the [2024 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament"). At the youth level, he led his team to two silver medals, including at the 2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup, where he set the FIBA record for blocks per game in a single tournament.
